raw_response_text:
{
  "project_id": "P-BFA-EconomicOpportunitiesResilience",
  "risks": [
    {
      "risk_id": "R01",
      "description": "Escalating insecurity and conflict may restrict access to target areas, delaying or halting project activities.",
      "category": "external",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Implement security SOPs, use remote delivery tools, partner with NGOs that have field access, and activate contingency plans for suspension if needed.",
      "evidence": "Annex 3 security risk matrix describing green/yellow/red risk levels and adaptations for economic inclusion and registry activities."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R02",
      "description": "Procurement delays caused by administrative routines and limited competition in fragile areas could affect timely delivery of goods and services.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Recruit a qualified procurement specialist, develop a detailed procurement procedures section in the PIM, and conduct fast‑track procurement trainings for DMP, DCMEF and bid committees.",
      "evidence": "Procurement risk assessment notes administrative routines may cause delays; limited bidders in fragile areas (section 83‑85)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R03",
      "description": "The newly created PIU lacks experienced financial management staff and systems, increasing fiduciary risk.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Recruit qualified FM staff by effectiveness, install approved accounting software, adopt a comprehensive FM manual, and engage an external auditor and internal audit arrangements.",
      "evidence": "FM assessment finds PIU has no FM staff, procedures, software; mitigation measures listed (section 82)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R04",
      "description": "Sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment (SEA/SH) incidents could arise among vulnerable beneficiaries, especially women and IDPs.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 5,
      "mitigation": "Implement an SEA/SH Action Plan with community sensitisation, a grievance mechanism, referral pathways to GBV services, and train all staff on code of conduct.",
      "evidence": "SEA/SH risk classified as Substantial; mitigation via Action Plan and Grievance Mechanism (section 87‑88)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R05",
      "description": "Construction of warehouses and logistics infrastructure may cause water and soil pollution.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Apply ESS 3 (pollution prevention) standards, conduct site‑specific environmental management plans, and monitor waste handling during construction.",
      "evidence": "E&S risks include water and soil pollution from construction sites (section 87)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R06",
      "description": "Interoperability of the RSU with other databases may breach data protection regulations, exposing personal data.",
      "category": "political_regulatory",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Engage the National Data Protection Authority to review data sharing protocols, implement encryption and access controls, and conduct privacy impact assessments.",
      "evidence": "Interoperability work will follow national data protection authority guidance (section 34‑35)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R07",
      "description": "Complex coordination among multiple ministries and partners could lead to fragmented implementation and duplication.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Establish a formal inter‑ministerial coordination unit, define clear roles in the PIM, and hold regular joint planning meetings.",
      "evidence": "Section 58‑59 notes fragmentation and need for stronger coordination mechanisms."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R08",
      "description": "Severe climate events (droughts, floods) may disrupt beneficiary participation and damage project assets.",
      "category": "environmental",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Integrate climate‑resilient livelihood packages, use early warning systems for shock‑responsive targeting, and design warehouses to withstand extreme weather.",
      "evidence": "Strategic context describes climate shocks and adaptation measures (section 2‑3, 77)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R09",
      "description": "Declining humanitarian funding could reduce complementary support for IDPs, affecting project outcomes.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Secure additional development financing through private sector partnerships, and build contingency buffers in the project budget for IDP‑specific activities.",
      "evidence": "Section 6 notes reduced humanitarian funding since 2025 and increased national ownership."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R10",
      "description": "Delay in recruiting key PIU staff (GBV specialist, security specialist, external auditor) may hinder compliance with legal covenants.",
      "category": "organizational",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Set firm recruitment timelines in the PIM, use competitive hiring processes, and monitor progress through quarterly PIU reports.",
      "evidence": "Legal covenants require recruitment within 3‑6 months after effectiveness (section FA Schedule 2)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R11",
      "description": "Women may face barriers to opening bank accounts (KYC) limiting financial inclusion benefits.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Partner with MFIs to simplify KYC procedures, provide ID document assistance, and offer mobile‑money alternatives where banking is limited.",
      "evidence": "Component 1.1 mentions gender‑sensitive adaptations such as daycare and KYC support (section 24‑25)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R12",
      "description": "Certain vulnerable groups (people with disabilities, elderly) may be excluded from RSU registration and benefits.",
      "category": "stakeholder",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Include explicit inclusion criteria in the proxy means test, conduct outreach through disability NGOs, and monitor disaggregated registration data.",
      "evidence": "RSU aims to cover female‑headed households, displaced persons, persons with disability (section 32)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R13",
      "description": "Fraud or corruption in procurement could undermine project credibility and financial integrity.",
      "category": "financial",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 4,
      "mitigation": "Apply World Bank anti‑corruption guidelines, conduct regular audits by ASCELC, and use FundsChain for real‑time tracking of disbursements.",
      "evidence": "Procurement risk includes fraud; fiduciary controls described in disbursement arrangements (section 70‑71)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R14",
      "description": "Security constraints may limit field monitoring, reducing data quality for M&E.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Utilise remote monitoring tools (GEMS, phone‑based PDM, IBM), and schedule periodic third‑party verification missions in accessible zones.",
      "evidence": "Monitoring plan mentions remote tools for insecure areas (section 67‑68, Annex 3)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R15",
      "description": "Roll‑out of the Unique Social Registry may be slower than planned, limiting beneficiary targeting.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Set phased rollout milestones, allocate dedicated staff for data collection, and monitor progress against a detailed implementation schedule.",
      "evidence": "RSU rollout targets 800,000 households; timeline described in Subcomponent 2.1 (section 32‑33)."
    },
    {
      "risk_id": "R16",
      "description": "Failure to achieve system interoperability could result in duplicate beneficiary records and inefficient service delivery.",
      "category": "technical",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 3,
      "mitigation": "Develop a clear interoperability architecture, conduct regular data reconciliation tests, and enforce standardized data exchange protocols.",
      "evidence": "Subcomponent 2.2 outlines need for interoperable framework and data exchange (section 34‑36)."
    }
  ]
}

risks.description: Escalating insecurity and conflict may restrict access to target areas, delaying or halting project activities.
risks.mitigation: Implement security SOPs, use remote delivery tools, partner with NGOs that have field access, and activate contingency plans for suspension if needed.
risks.evidence: Annex 3 security risk matrix describing green/yellow/red risk levels and adaptations for economic inclusion and registry activities.

risks.description: Procurement delays caused by administrative routines and limited competition in fragile areas could affect timely delivery of goods and services.
risks.mitigation: Recruit a qualified procurement specialist, develop a detailed procurement procedures section in the PIM, and conduct fast‑track procurement trainings for DMP, DCMEF and bid committees.
risks.evidence: Procurement risk assessment notes administrative routines may cause delays; limited bidders in fragile areas (section 83‑85).

risks.description: The newly created PIU lacks experienced financial management staff and systems, increasing fiduciary risk.
risks.mitigation: Recruit qualified FM staff by effectiveness, install approved accounting software, adopt a comprehensive FM manual, and engage an external auditor and internal audit arrangements.
risks.evidence: FM assessment finds PIU has no FM staff, procedures, software; mitigation measures listed (section 82).

risks.description: Sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment (SEA/SH) incidents could arise among vulnerable beneficiaries, especially women and IDPs.
risks.mitigation: Implement an SEA/SH Action Plan with community sensitisation, a grievance mechanism, referral pathways to GBV services, and train all staff on code of conduct.
risks.evidence: SEA/SH risk classified as Substantial; mitigation via Action Plan and Grievance Mechanism (section 87‑88).

risks.description: Construction of warehouses and logistics infrastructure may cause water and soil pollution.
risks.mitigation: Apply ESS 3 (pollution prevention) standards, conduct site‑specific environmental management plans, and monitor waste handling during construction.
risks.evidence: E&S risks include water and soil pollution from construction sites (section 87).

risks.description: Interoperability of the RSU with other databases may breach data protection regulations, exposing personal data.
risks.mitigation: Engage the National Data Protection Authority to review data sharing protocols, implement encryption and access controls, and conduct privacy impact assessments.
risks.evidence: Interoperability work will follow national data protection authority guidance (section 34‑35).

risks.description: Complex coordination among multiple ministries and partners could lead to fragmented implementation and duplication.
risks.mitigation: Establish a formal inter‑ministerial coordination unit, define clear roles in the PIM, and hold regular joint planning meetings.
risks.evidence: Section 58‑59 notes fragmentation and need for stronger coordination mechanisms.

risks.description: Severe climate events (droughts, floods) may disrupt beneficiary participation and damage project assets.
risks.mitigation: Integrate climate‑resilient livelihood packages, use early warning systems for shock‑responsive targeting, and design warehouses to withstand extreme weather.
risks.evidence: Strategic context describes climate shocks and adaptation measures (section 2‑3, 77).

risks.description: Declining humanitarian funding could reduce complementary support for IDPs, affecting project outcomes.
risks.mitigation: Secure additional development financing through private sector partnerships, and build contingency buffers in the project budget for IDP‑specific activities.
risks.evidence: Section 6 notes reduced humanitarian funding since 2025 and increased national ownership.

risks.description: Delay in recruiting key PIU staff (GBV specialist, security specialist, external auditor) may hinder compliance with legal covenants.
risks.mitigation: Set firm recruitment timelines in the PIM, use competitive hiring processes, and monitor progress through quarterly PIU reports.
risks.evidence: Legal covenants require recruitment within 3‑6 months after effectiveness (section FA Schedule 2).

risks.description: Women may face barriers to opening bank accounts (KYC) limiting financial inclusion benefits.
risks.mitigation: Partner with MFIs to simplify KYC procedures, provide ID document assistance, and offer mobile‑money alternatives where banking is limited.
risks.evidence: Component 1.1 mentions gender‑sensitive adaptations such as daycare and KYC support (section 24‑25).

risks.description: Certain vulnerable groups (people with disabilities, elderly) may be excluded from RSU registration and benefits.
risks.mitigation: Include explicit inclusion criteria in the proxy means test, conduct outreach through disability NGOs, and monitor disaggregated registration data.
risks.evidence: RSU aims to cover female‑headed households, displaced persons, persons with disability (section 32).

risks.description: Fraud or corruption in procurement could undermine project credibility and financial integrity.
risks.mitigation: Apply World Bank anti‑corruption guidelines, conduct regular audits by ASCELC, and use FundsChain for real‑time tracking of disbursements.
risks.evidence: Procurement risk includes fraud; fiduciary controls described in disbursement arrangements (section 70‑71).

risks.description: Security constraints may limit field monitoring, reducing data quality for M&E.
risks.mitigation: Utilise remote monitoring tools (GEMS, phone‑based PDM, IBM), and schedule periodic third‑party verification missions in accessible zones.
risks.evidence: Monitoring plan mentions remote tools for insecure areas (section 67‑68, Annex 3).

risks.description: Roll‑out of the Unique Social Registry may be slower than planned, limiting beneficiary targeting.
risks.mitigation: Set phased rollout milestones, allocate dedicated staff for data collection, and monitor progress against a detailed implementation schedule.
risks.evidence: RSU rollout targets 800,000 households; timeline described in Subcomponent 2.1 (section 32‑33).

risks.description: Failure to achieve system interoperability could result in duplicate beneficiary records and inefficient service delivery.
risks.mitigation: Develop a clear interoperability architecture, conduct regular data reconciliation tests, and enforce standardized data exchange protocols.
risks.evidence: Subcomponent 2.2 outlines need for interoperable framework and data exchange (section 34‑36).
